title: Security lab ground truth
note: Every vulnerability planted in the security lab, written down before QA NXT ran against it. A scanner verified against an application whose flaws nobody enumerated first is a scanner verified against its own output. The safeEndpoints are not filler: they are how precision is measured, and a finding reported against one of them is a false positive by definition rather than by argument.
principles: Local only. Every application binds to 127.0.0.1 and none makes an outbound request.
Synthetic only. No credential, account, balance or file here corresponds to anything real.
Nothing persists. No database, no shell, no filesystem writes — only the observable behaviour of applications that have them.

expectedFindings.detectBy: The response distinguishes an unknown username from a wrong password.
Repeated failed sign-ins are never throttled.
A token captured before sign-out still authenticates after it.
expiresInSeconds is 30 days.
The same reset token is accepted twice.

safeEndpoints.why: Answers 202 whether or not the account exists, so it does not enumerate. Reporting enumeration here is a false positive.

expectedFindings.detectBy: alice receives acc-1002, which bob owns.
A customer receives 200 from an admin route.
A readonly account receives 201.
An unauthenticated caller receives a statement.

safeEndpoints.why: Returns only the caller's own accounts. Reporting BOLA here is a false positive.

expectedFindings.detectBy: A forged bearer value naming another user is accepted.
A customer sets their own role.
A non-string, an empty value and an oversized value are all accepted.
DELETE succeeds unauthenticated.

expectedFindings.severityNote: Recorded as low when this file was first written, which was a casual label rather than a derived one. The severity model scores it medium from its factors: trivially exploitable, no account required, publicly reachable. The label was raised to match the factors rather than the factors bent to match the label.
expectedFindings.detectBy: More than 10 requests are never refused.
Password hashes and API tokens appear in the response.

safeEndpoints.why: Enforces ownership correctly. Reporting BOLA here is a false positive.

expectedFindings.detectBy: The marker is returned into an HTML context with its angle brackets intact.
A marker stored once is rendered unencoded on a later read.
location.hash reaches innerHTML; visible only in a browser, not in the response body.
expectedFindings.severityNote: Raised from medium. On every axis of the severity model this is the same vulnerability as VULN_REFLECTED_XSS on the same page: a crafted link, script running in the origin as the victim, no account needed, reaching whatever the page reaches, publicly addressable. Producing a lower band required asserting that it needs conditions reflected XSS does not, which is not true — both need a victim to open a link. The earlier medium was a number with no factors behind it, which is what this model exists to replace.

safeEndpoints.why: Reflects HTML-escaped. Reporting XSS on reflection alone is a false positive, and the brief names this case explicitly.
Reflects into JSON, which is not an HTML context. A scanner flagging it does not understand context.

expectedFindings.detectBy: A state-changing request succeeds with no anti-CSRF token.
A cross-origin Origin header is accepted.
An executable extension and a mismatched content type are accepted.
A declared size far above the limit is accepted.
storedAs retains ../ from the supplied filename.
An absolute external URL is returned in Location.
A loopback and a private-range destination are both accepted rather than refused. Nothing is actually fetched by the lab, and the metadata endpoints are never probed by default.

safeEndpoints.why: The application's own origin is a legitimate destination. Reporting SSRF for an endpoint that accepts only itself is a false positive.

expectedFindings.detectBy: No Content-Security-Policy on an HTML response.
A session cookie with no HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite.
An arbitrary Origin is reflected while credentials are allowed. Both together, not either alone.
A directory index naming backup.sql and .env.
A stack trace naming source paths, host and framework version.
A source map with sourcesContent is served.

safeEndpoints.why: Every header set and the cookie correctly attributed. Any header or cookie finding here is a false positive.
A wildcard origin with no credentials on genuinely public data. Correct, and commonly mis-flagged — the brief says not to classify every permissive CORS policy as a vulnerability.

expectedFindings.detectBy: An unbalanced quote produces a database error; a tautology widens the result from 0 rows to 3. Detection only — no extraction is attempted.
An operator object is accepted where a string belongs.
A metacharacter produces a shell-shaped error. Nothing is executed.
{{7*7}} renders as 49.
